# Reused OMP sources

Standalone vanilla-player extension: PreviewVanillaModel supplies real six-part inner and outer-layer player geometry, standard skin UV regions and separate classic/slim arm dimensions. It uses the existing independent part/palette path rather than empty VanillaModelAPI objects; supported player visibility members/groups affect rendering, and an entirely hidden player omits its draw submission. This is a neutral player pose with supported Lua transforms, not the complete Minecraft equipment/pose host. Default Steve/Alex PNGs are read from the same installed Minecraft JAR and included under their original assets/minecraft paths with provenance hashes. User HTTP(S) skins remain in a persistent adjacent cache, not bundled third-party avatar content. Pixel detection uses the transparent unused slim-arm strips; explicit model selection remains available. Skin bytes/hash and cache source are recorded.

World-clock/math-library update: the original `refs/Figura_Orig/common/src/main/resources/assets/figura/scripts/math.lua` is copied unchanged to `resources/assets/omni-morph/scripts/math.lua` and packaged inside the JAR. It is loaded after original vector registration, retaining Lua scalar/vector helpers and scale constants. PreviewWorldClock adapts WorldAPI.getTime/getTimeOfDay's tick-plus-delta semantics to the actual standalone 20 Hz script event counter, with explicit configurable initial game/day ticks; day time is not silently wrapped. It does not provide a fake block/entity world or claim those APIs are implemented.

Keybind update: FiguraKeybind and KeybindAPI are copied from `refs/Figura_Orig/.../lua/api/keybind/`. Avatar becomes PreviewLua; callbacks execute with the real bounded host, preserving original modifier/binding arguments, callback-before-isDown update, edge detection, override results, aliases, enable/GUI/rebind and field assignment behavior. InputConstants.Key becomes PreviewKeys.Key mapped to actual GLFW keyboard/mouse/scancode identifiers, compared by device/code rather than object identity. Minecraft live polling is replaced by queued GLFW input and explicit reproducible configuration; focus loss/close release actual bindings. GUI gating uses explicit standalone simulated GUI state. Vanilla mapping lookup requires configured identifiers rather than a Minecraft singleton; key display names remain identifiers. No fake key events or empty callbacks supply test results.

Vector and simulated-host update: FiguraVector/Vec2/Vec3/Vec4 and FiguraMatrix/Mat2/Mat3/Mat4, VectorsAPI and MatricesAPI are copied from the same `refs/Figura_Orig` reference. Arithmetic, operators, swizzles, matrix conventions and public mathematical methods are preserved. Live Minecraft BlockPos/Vec3 conversion methods are omitted; JOML conversion remains. Pure LuaUtils argument conversion and MathUtils/ColorUtils helpers are extracted into PreviewVectorArguments/PreviewVectorMath; Pair becomes a concrete local value record. Formatting uses a thread-local decimal formatter instead of the game chat printer. The original Figura color constants and standard formatting-color RGB values preserve named-color parsing without chat objects. The two camera-dependent vector helpers explicitly reject calls until the actual preview camera host is connected. PreviewSimulatedApi supplies only explicit typed configured player reads with fresh vectors; unconfigured state errors rather than supplying invented values. Local pings are actual instance Lua callbacks, with no network host. Part scalar/vector setters and copy-returning getters use the original conversion rules. Full keybind, particle/sound, world/entity and camera hosts remain pending.

Figura animation update (2026-11-07): Animation, AnimationPlayer, Interpolation, TransformType and AnimationAPI are copied from `refs/Figura_Orig/common/src/main/java/org/figuramc/figura/` (same PolyForm Noncommercial license in that reference). Animation replaces Avatar with PreviewLua and its bounded compilation/callback host, propagating failures; its playback API, code-frame windows, delays, loop modes, speed, pause and priority are retained. AnimationPlayer removes live profiling and uses a local lower-bound search and actual PreviewFiguraParts.Part transforms. Interpolation uses JOML double vectors with the original scalar Catmull-Rom/Bezier formulas extracted into FiguraAnimationMath. TimeController retains pause bookkeeping with a configured simulation clock and clamps seek-replay steps before an input's start. Keyframe adapts original pre/end, cached numeric/expression/block Lua and Bezier handle semantics to the parser's actual typed tags; it propagates errors instead of substituting zero. AnimationAPI replaces only the owner type. Shared parser metadata is retained; clocks, compiled Lua, priorities and part contributions are per instance. Fixed-time playback replays original animation updates at 60 Hz to retain loop timeline events. Original animation override flags still describe vanilla-parent transforms, whose full simulated host remains pending; no fake Minecraft parent transforms are supplied. Dynamic bbmodel Molang properties remain explicitly unsupported until connected.

Source: local reference `refs/OMP/OMP_26.3/common/src/main/java/top/aihmc/omnimorph/`.
License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, reproduced in LICENSE.md and included in the preview JAR.

The YSM geometry parser, geometry DTOs, manifest resource semantics and directory/ZIP container are reused here.
`YsmPackage` and `YsmManifestReader` use the preview's concrete filesystem helper `ResourcePaths` in place of the Minecraft-dependent IOUtils class.
The manifest reader's list-only metadata and encrypted-path convenience overloads are omitted; its resource-source parser is preserved.
The encrypted source, crypto decoders (including their Sparkle-Morpher notice), binary reader/geometry mapper, bounded texture decoder and FiguraAvifDecoder lifecycle adapter are reused unchanged. The AVIF adapter originates at `common/src/main/java/com/github/ustc_zzzz/imageio/avif/`.

No Molang, Lua or image-decoder stubs are included. Static preview uses ImageIO for ordinary package PNG textures, and the original decoder for encrypted binary RGBA/encoded textures. Runtime dependency JARs retain their upstream license entries; see their bundled META-INF notices.

Figura parser sources originate at `common/src/main/java/org/figuramc/figura/parsers/`: BlockbenchParser2, BlockbenchCommonTypes, BlockbenchV4Model, BlockbenchV5Model, GsonTypeByField and ModelParseResult. ParentType originates at `org/figuramc/figura/model/`.
Their parsing logic remains in the original classes. Minecraft NBT imports are redirected to the preview's functional typed in-memory data tree (including numeric widths and byte arrays); no NBT binary serialization is needed. IOUtils operations and UUID conversion use ResourcePaths. FiguraMod logging uses PreviewDiagnostics; an unused legacy parser import is removed. ParentType retains its aliases/flags/offsets, with JOML vectors and an enum of host body-part names in place of the Minecraft provider objects. These metadata names do not launch Minecraft or provide its live state.
The standalone geometry upload adapter uses cube face/UV ordering and group-versus-mesh rotation order from FiguraModelPartReader and PartCustomization. Weighted armature skinning is explicitly rejected until connected, rather than silently drawing rigid substitutes.

The Molang lexer/parser/AST/evaluator and execution budget originate at `top/aihmc/omnimorph/molang/`; Minecraft-dependent MolangBindings and QueryVariables are excluded. PreviewMathBinding extracts the original MathBinding namespace registrations. MathFunctions retains the original function bodies, substituting PreviewMath for the three arithmetic helpers and a per-instance seeded java.util.Random for the live Avatar random source. PreviewMolang supplies actual configured query values, clocks and separate writable variable stores. Missing host queries throw a diagnostic rather than returning simulated zero values implicitly.

The YSM animation parser, channel/keyframe/clip/event/pose DTOs, easing and sampler originate at `top/aihmc/omnimorph/model/ysm/animation/`. Default Avatar-engine overloads are omitted in favor of explicit engine injection. The sampler's live Avatar bone-filter scope is omitted; unsupported host calls are diagnosed by the standalone binding layer. Parser/channel/blend exceptions propagate instead of silently substituting empty clips or numeric fallbacks. The sampler/easing and finite-value hold behavior otherwise remain from the original code. YsmBinaryAnimationMapper is reused unchanged for encrypted binary animation resources. PreviewAnimation applies the original YsmRenderer animation-axis signs and transform order, executes chronological Molang timeline events, and owns separate playback/pose/palette state per instance. Named-clip mode remains separate from declared-controller playback; non-Molang events are not yet connected.

YsmVisibilityDefaults adapts YsmAnimationPlayer's isBaseAnimation/isParallelSlot/isZeroScaleChannel/scaleMagnitude rules. Only literal scale channels enter this static default analysis, via the real YsmAnimationParser and sampler; dynamically evaluated scale is excluded as in OMP. Resource merging follows YsmModelRuntime.mergeAnimations (later declared clip wins). The original YsmManifestReader.firstPersonAnimationPaths helper is exposed publicly to keep the main/first-person resource split; encrypted type11 uses the same split. Geometry is retained so a later action or setting can show attachments again. Initial-controller visibility now reuses YsmAnimationControllerParser and its controller/state/reference/transition/slot/blend DTOs. The parser requires an explicit real engine, removes Avatar defaults, and propagates invalid expressions rather than replacing them with constants or empty lists. The visibility adapter retains only initial references to clips with literal constant-zero scales; runtime transitions and entry/exit expressions are not executed by static visibility analysis. Conditional references are evaluated against each instance host; full controller playback remains pending.


YsmControllerRuntime and YsmControllerPoseLayer originate in `top/aihmc/omnimorph/model/ysm/controller/`. The pose layer is reused unchanged. The runtime uses PreviewMolang/PreviewControllerPlayer instead of live Avatar/YsmAnimationPlayer, retains its original state/transition/child/context algorithm, and propagates execution failures. Sound and function dispatch hooks are omitted only for this currently admitted subset: controller playback rejects sound events/state sounds, ysm-builtin states, root functions/action schemas and separately declared package/binary function resources. PreviewControllerPlayer owns actual slot clocks, timeline execution, finite pose caches, completion status, start poses and controller transition layers; no live-Minecraft or empty parser/evaluator stubs supply those values. Full sound/function/builtin hosting remains required before complete asset benchmarks are enabled.


Figura Lua hosting now uses the actual cached FiguraMC LuaJ core/jse 3.0.8-figura JARs. LuaWhitelist/LuaNotNil and the Lua documentation annotations, ReadOnlyLuaTable, PathUtils, AvatarControlDefinition and AvatarControlType are reused from the same OMP reference. The original sandbox.lua is packaged unchanged at assets/omni-morph/scripts/sandbox.lua. LuaEvent keeps its queue/register/remove/call behavior with only live profiler calls removed; EventsAPI omits mod entrypoint discovery and otherwise retains the built-in events and assignment rules. LuaTypeManager retains whitelist/metatable/argument conversion, replacing documentation display names with local type names and omitting Minecraft Component JSON conversion; a demonstrated model enum options failure adds Lua table-to-List conversion. Java Error causes pass through reflection so a VM instruction-budget signal cannot be swallowed by Lua pcall. AvatarControlsAPI retains its factories/aliases, replacing Avatar with PreviewLua and routing openPage to standalone selected-page state (settings UI remains pending).

PreviewLua adapts FiguraLuaRuntime's library/compiler setup, debug-hook instruction accounting, module cache/circular dependency detection and relative require behavior. Globals, modules, RNG and controls are per instance. It executes real init/tick/render/post-render callbacks and passes configured simulated states; it does not expose empty Minecraft API implementations. PreviewControlRuntime adapts the original AvatarControlRuntime value/interceptor/binding/change/press/reset ordering, enum option commands and roaming aliases to an actual PreviewMolang VariableStorage. It does not yet provide original disk persistence or live binding hydration. Script execution is opt-in and currently reaches YSM animation/controller palettes through original Molang bindings; full Figura model-part/animation APIs, wheel/settings UI and the remaining model host APIs are still required before full benchmarks are admitted.


ActionWheelAPI, Page and Action originate at `org/figuramc/figura/lua/api/action_wheel/`. Page is reused unchanged. ActionWheelAPI replaces the live Avatar/global GUI wheel with the same instance's PreviewLua wheel state/dispatch. Action preserves original click, right-click, toggle/untoggle, scroll, callbacks, titles, page requests and field/metamethod behavior; Avatar.run's instruction-budget parameter is supplied by PreviewLua's actual bounded owner rather than passed as a Lua argument. Item values are retained as identifier strings and displayed as metadata; wheel colors use a concrete standalone RGB value consumed by the real UI. Live Minecraft item objects, FiguraTexture setters/TextureData and YSM held-input adapter are not included in this current subset. Declarative ysmAction dispatch fails explicitly until its real host is connected. The standalone dispatch keeps the original GUI ActionWheel global interception/action/scroll/page-group order. Texture/item icon rendering and full vector/model APIs remain pending; no complete asset benchmark is claimed.
Latest adaptation update: YsmActionDefinition is reused unchanged. YsmActionRuntime substitutes PreviewYsmRuntime/PreviewActionPlayer and simulated ticks for live model/player/global ticks; Minecraft network recording is omitted. Original action selection, cooldown, speed, toggle and held-Press generation ownership are retained. YsmActionSchemaParser retains original schema/property/form interpretation with the standalone facade and propagating diagnostics. AvatarTranslations retains UTF-8 dictionaries and locale fallback with an explicit locale, omitting Minecraft/NBT entry points. PreviewYsmResources extracts the original YsmBinaryMetadataMapper properties mapping without its image sink. PreviewYsmRuntime adapts the original automatic action-wheel layout without reading the mod's saved layout. PreviewActionPlayer adapts actual direct playback/timeline/pose composition. Action held-input and real ysmAction dispatch are now connected; earlier statements that these are omitted are superseded. PreviewControlRuntime now performs live binding hydration; original disk persistence remains pending. No Minecraft process or network stub supplies model state.
Figura model-part integration update: the original BlockbenchParser2 output is retained as a hierarchy with owner indices rather than discarded after bind baking. PreviewFiguraParts is a standalone adapter for scalar model-part transform setters, using the original FiguraModelPartReader initial rotation/pivot/visibility and PartCustomization pivot/scale/mesh versus group rotation conventions. It does not copy the live Minecraft FiguraModelPart host or claim its full API. Actual Lua models hierarchy, settings and wheel callbacks feed per-instance matrices; original-parser global material indices are retained. Full keyframe animation and vector/model APIs remain pending.
`PreviewFiguraParts.Part.partToWorldMatrix` follows the original FiguraModelPart savedPartToWorldMat copy contract. The snapshot is updated during actual hierarchy/palette composition using the pivot-relative pixel-to-block transform, matching ImmediateAvatarRenderer semantics for the preview model coordinate space. It does not supply Minecraft camera/player world placement.

ParticleAPI and LuaParticle are adapted from refs/Figura_Orig/common/src/main/java/org/figuramc/figura/lua/api/particle/. Original public Lua methods, aliases, vector conversion, copy-returning getters, lifetime clamping, power and scale wrapper semantics are retained; Minecraft Particle/ParticleEngine/Avatar and permission/pause state are replaced by the instance-local PreviewParticles backend. Documentation-only overload annotations are shortened; whitelisted runtime signatures remain. The needed parseVec4 conversion is copied from original LuaUtils into PreviewVectorArguments. The backend is a deterministic standalone six-type preview simulation, not a vendored Minecraft particle engine: it uses a flat ground plane, configured global water, and deterministic leaf wind. ParticleRenderer submits actual sorted billboard triangles with original Minecraft particle definitions/sprites. Build-Preview extracts six JSON definitions and 41 extra PNGs from the installed game JAR and records their hashes; those assets remain generated build outputs. No silent unsupported-type or spawn implementation is supplied.

SoundAPI and LuaSound originate in refs/Figura_Orig/common/src/main/java/org/figuramc/figura/lua/api/sound/. Public whitelisted names/aliases, vector/scalar playSound parsing, newSound base64/byte-table decoding, position/volume/pitch/attenuation/loop fields and play/pause/resume/stop flow are adapted to PreviewSounds/PreviewAudio. Documentation-only overload annotations are shortened. Live Minecraft SoundEngine/Avatar/permissions/global categories are replaced by per-instance ownership and an actual shared OpenAL device, with STB Vorbis PCM decoding and content-addressed buffer sharing. ON_PLAY_SOUND callbacks/cancellation dispatch locally, not across live avatars; variant selection is seeded. Unknown/unpackaged sounds report errors rather than silently producing an empty LuaSound. Subtitles are text properties, without Minecraft component translation/rendering. Audio currently uses complete mono/stereo static buffers, not Minecraft streaming channels. Build-Preview reads selected original event definitions and hashed OGG objects from an existing installed Minecraft asset cache, keeping source metadata in generated JAR assets. No new audio server/device package, empty playback host or game process is used.

Persistence update: PreviewSettings adapts AvatarControlValueStore's persistent-type filtering, apply/restore order, typed scalar values and YSM enum-index rule from refs/OMP/OMP_26.3/common/src/main/java/top/aihmc/omnimorph/avatar/control/AvatarControlValueStore.java. Minecraft owner/model/NBT-cache storage is replaced by model/engine-scoped JSON files with hashed identities and atomic file replacement. Figura enums retain their original label values for script compatibility. PreviewControlRuntime applies saved values during registration and before initial binding hydration; accepted changes save after binding sync and before callbacks, while intercepted changes do not save. The reused AvatarControlDefinition.setPersistent(false) now discards only a pending restored value, so chained author metadata can opt out after registration without overwriting an explicit author value. All other original definition formatting/source is retained. Benchmark mode never reads/writes preference state; explicit controls remain reproducible. These updates supersede earlier notes that disk persistence is pending.
Exit lifecycle correction: PreviewMain finishes actual input-release callbacks before closing the model audio runtime and writing final settings/audio records. GLFW still completes its native cleanup before the Swing companion is released. A held-key release callback that saves a control and plays sound is covered by a real-window regression.

YSM sound hosting supersedes earlier sound exclusions: YsmAnimationEventWindow and YsmControllerSoundBank are reused unchanged. YsmAnimationClip exposes orderedEvents publicly; YsmControllerRuntime restores state-entry/exit sound ownership hooks through PreviewControllerPlayer. PreviewYsmEffects executes actual timeline expressions and native audio events for named clips, controller states and declared actions, retaining the original playback-step clock and strict loop-end crossing. Function resources, builtin states and other event kinds remain explicitly unsupported.

YsmAudioDecoder is adapted from OMP's model/ysm/YsmAudioDecoder.java. The bounded Opus path, pre-skip, output gain, stereo downmix and final granule trimming are retained using vorbis-java-core 0.8 and Concentus 1.0.2. Minecraft JOrbisAudioStream is replaced by bounded LWJGL STB Vorbis chunk decoding with the same mono PCM output contract. Model audio uses a distinct shared buffer cache profile; Figura's existing mono/stereo Vorbis API remains separate. Both dependency JARs are packaged with the preview dependencies and their embedded notices/licenses.

YSM standalone function hosting: YsmMolangFunctionName, YsmFunctionEventBus, YsmControllerSlotBinder are reused unchanged. TempVariableStorage adds only clearFrame to reset values and scopes while retaining its allocated backing array. PreviewYsmFunctions adapts OMP YsmMolangFunctionRuntime's named call, argument struct, event ordering/bus, controller-scoped dispatch, call frames and temporary scope execution to PreviewMolang. NBT resource loading is replaced by retained source strings; live Avatar/model and multiplayer sync plumbing is omitted. Missing named functions, parse failures and execution errors propagate instead of returning silent zero. The original recursion limit and evaluator execution budget apply. FnBinding/args and ysm.event/run_event/trigger_event use the same argument-offset conventions. PreviewControllerPlayer restores original controller-stage dispatch and synthesizes missing stage controllers through the unchanged original binder. Deferred/network functions and builtin states remain unsupported; no empty host supplies their results.

YSM function sound hosting: PreviewYsmSoundFunctions adapts YsmSoundRuntime. Original ID conversion, anonymous/indexed banks, replace/global/loop flags, local/controller/global bank selection, owner-scoped stop and playback transfer remain. Live Entity position/removal is replaced by the configured preview position and explicit model/playback lifetime; model audio is created through the actual PreviewSounds/OpenAL backend. The mod's isPreviewRuntime gate is intentionally omitted because this standalone preview explicitly supports real audio. PreviewYsmFunctions restores nested client-effect ownership scopes; timeline, controller-stage and state-entry/exit effects execute only within those scopes. Existing execution budgets are retained alongside effect scopes.

YsmFilterRuntime is reused unchanged. PreviewMolang exposes original first_order/second_order argument defaults in the PREVIEW domain. PreviewAnimation updates filters once per submitted model frame using monotonic simulation seconds converted to 20 Hz ticks, before parameter sampling; clip wrapping and controller substeps do not reset filter clocks. YsmAnimationSampler restores the original per-bone filter scope with PreviewMolang replacing Avatar.MolangContext; previously documented fail-fast channel evaluation remains. Instance and seek lifetime use independently owned filter runtimes.

YSM simulated equipment hosting: PreviewYsmEquipment follows MolangBindings.CtrlBinding equipmentFunction, handItem, armor, parseSlot and itemMatches. Minecraft LivingEntity/item registry/tag/type queries are replaced by explicit states.equipment JSON snapshots. Slot aliases, use/swing gating, empty/exact-ID/tag/type matching, armor restrictions and two-or-three argument validation remain. The caller supplies actual classification metadata; item IDs are not substring-classified and no Minecraft process is used. Missing required simulated values fail with their configuration path.

Local YSM sync hosting: PreviewYsmFunctions.recordSync adapts the original YsmMolangFunctionRuntime local callback path: client-effect gate, at most sixteen converted finite floats, bounded recent history and immediate ordered @sync handler execution with original argument/temp scopes. Network capture/transmission and remote replay are omitted for this standalone runtime; local callbacks execute real model code rather than a no-op sync stub. Original Molang NaN-to-zero numeric conversion remains, while infinity is rejected by the original finite check.

Controller function playback: PreviewYsmControllerFunctions adapts MolangBindings.CtrlBinding's context gate, set_animation/reset/set_beginning_transition_length/indicate_reload bindings, loop-mode constants and argument contracts. PreviewControllerPlayer adapts YsmAnimationPlayer's controller-function slot identity, persistent selection/transition lengths, queued reload, retirement and clock/initial-event delay. Repeated selection keeps the playback and its voices; reload creates a new owner and retires the previous one; reset stops owned audio and retires the previous slot. Retired slots are excluded from sampling; outgoing snapshots belong to the original pose layer, and channels absent from the incoming pose return to lower layers immediately. Creation during controller updates defers that update's timeline advance. A positive beginning transition freezes function clock/events until its boundary; only remaining time after the boundary advances the clip. Function LOOP samples retain the exact endpoint until strictly crossed. Declared-controller slots now use the same original beginning-delay and creation-frame deferral protocol, including delayed initial events and remaining-delta advancement. This does not add first-person rendering. YsmControllerRuntime restores the original function-playback contribution to controller clocks/completion flags.

Executable lifecycle: PreviewMain.main now explicitly owns the standalone JAR process. It calls run(), waits for existing window/model/audio/input cleanup and final writes, then requests normal JVM shutdown through System.exit(0); an exception is printed and exits with status 1 after run's finally blocks. This addresses observed completed JAR runs remaining alive in AWT-Shutdown/DestroyJavaVM after disposal. It does not change internal AWT flags, terminate another process, bypass resource cleanup, or claim to fix JDK automatic AWT shutdown. Reusable rendering/host classes do not terminate the process. Regression checks include actual successful windows and an intentionally failing real-window script, its nonzero exit and finalized cleanup records.

Relative block tag hosting: PreviewBlockQueries adapts QueryVariables.worldTagFunction(true,false) and relativeQueryPosition. Original <=5 per-axis offset bounds, finite checks, Math.round(entity position + offset - 0.5), world-axis coordinates without yaw rotation, ANY-tag short-circuiting and Identifier-style namespace validation are retained. Minecraft level/tag registry access is replaced by explicit states.world.blocks/defaultBlockTags snapshots; player position uses states.player.pos or the preview model origin. Missing sampled block metadata fails explicitly. This simulation does not infer block tags from rendered ground textures or claim to implement a Minecraft world.

YSM bone vector hosting: PreviewYsmBones adapts YsmBoneQuery's read-only x/y/z Struct, live copy semantics and model-channel signs/units, and YsmBoneQueryRuntime's previous-complete-frame input snapshot/evaluation scope algorithm. The actual standalone sampled pose channels replace YsmModelPart raw fields; no additional user part transforms exist in this host. Inputs remain frozen throughout one frame's callbacks/controllers/bone sampling and duplicate frame IDs, while completed output is published only after successful evaluation. Outside evaluation, saved Struct views observe current complete outputs. Seek reconstructs the entire owner. Vanilla player appendices are excluded through their actual skeleton offset. Position/rotation/scale use this snapshot protocol; tracked pivots use the separate original render-time protocol described below. First-person bone querying remains unimplemented. This supersedes any prior suggestion that these bone queries were unavailable.


YSM particle emission: PreviewYsmParticles adapts YsmParticleRequest.parse/emit from common/src/main/java/top/aihmc/omnimorph/model/ysm/YsmParticleRequest.java and the client-effects ownership gate from YsmParticleRuntime.execute. It retains optional numeric defaults, count/lifetime limits, single versus Gaussian batch velocity, player-body versus entity yaw selection, Vec3.yRot coordinate signs and absolute-mode offset behavior. Minecraft vectors, registry/dispatch and entity state are replaced by JOML values, an explicit simulated player snapshot and the existing real standalone particle simulation/renderer. The standalone loop executes synchronously and has no deferred cross-thread dispatch queue. Per-model seeded Gaussian randomness is reproducible; only the existing six standalone particle implementations are supported, with explicit errors for unavailable types. Lua and YSM share their model's live particle storage; no-Lua YSM particles tick and draw directly. Shutdown/seek closes the old particle owner. This does not claim a Minecraft particle engine, non-player entities or support for arbitrary parameterized particle options.


YSM input hosting: PreviewYsmInput adapts the numeric key/button arrays, range checks, ANY-key query and readiness-clearing behavior of common/src/main/java/top/aihmc/omnimorph/model/ysm/YsmInputState.java, together with MolangBindings.inputFunction argument arities and ownership gate. Offline states.input.owner/ready/keys/mouse replace Minecraft local-player identity, overlay/screen/mouse-grab/window readiness. Actual GLFW focus/key/button events and existing recorded interaction operations update the same per-model state, including without a Lua VM. Scancode and Figura modifier callbacks remain separate from YSM's numeric GLFW queries. Hand-action state is not inferred from this input adapter; the existing explicit equipment/action simulation remains responsible. This does not implement Minecraft's global DEVICE, multiplayer entities or game GUI state.

Keyboard repeat events retain an explicit recorded repeat flag: the existing Figura path is preserved, while YSM ignores them like YsmInputState.keyEvent(action=2).


Tracked YSM pivots: PreviewYsmBones adapts YsmBoneQueryRuntime.trackPivot/read/recordPivot and YsmRenderer.updateTrackedPivots/updateTrackedPivot. Registration initializes a tracked vector to zero; only visible branches with nonzero scale on every axis are updated at the model render boundary. Hidden branches retain their previous finite values. The actual computed preview hierarchy matrices transform each bone pivot, then the root width/height controls are removed and coordinates converted to original model pixels (-X,+Y,+Z). Like the original renderer's identity-root tracking walk, this excludes global model scale, entity/world and camera transforms. Pivot reads are live render-tracked values rather than ordinary channel input snapshots. No first-person or direct Lua part transforms are added by this change. This supersedes prior suggestions that abs meant world position or remained unsupported.


Simulated controller arguments: states.ctrl supplies per-instance scalar controller values directly. No Minecraft movement/hand state selector, default MAIN/ARM animation library or automatic base/hold/use/swing playback is included. Model-authored controllers and animations remain responsible for their own transitions and poses.

Script discovery update: PreviewLua.listFiles reuses OMP_26.3 FiguraLuaRuntime.listFiles path normalization, relative-directory, recursion, module-name and argument semantics over the actual immutable Program.sources inventory. It does not enumerate host filesystem paths or supply fake module lists.

Client version update: Version.java is copied unchanged from OMP_26.3 org/figuramc/figura/utils. PreviewClient.compareVersions retains ClientAPI's actual parse/invalid-version/comparison path. getFiguraVersion reads an explicit states.client.getFiguraVersion simulation value; the standalone tool does not claim to run the whole Figura/Minecraft client.

Avatar metadata update: PreviewAvatarData follows OMP AvatarAPI.getNBT and NbtToLua.convert, converting the actual retained parser model hierarchy and animation/timeline records into fresh Lua tables. PreviewTags numeric/string/compound/list/byte-array/int-array cases replace Minecraft NBT types. It exposes retained preview model/animation sections, not fabricated scripts, texture bytes or a Minecraft entity NBT host.

Runtime metatable update: PreviewLua reuses OMP FiguraLuaRuntime.loadExtraLibraries type/pairs/ipairs dispatch and LuaTypeManager.dumpMetatables over its actual registered types. Model attachment refreshes the exported registry before script initialization. Each runtime retains its original independent metatables; no model-specific patch or extra game state machine is introduced.

Wheel color correction: the earlier preview-only Color record reused the Vector3 documentation name and conflicted with the actual FiguraVec3 metatable. Action color fields/arguments now use the original FiguraVec3 type and real vector operations; the preview color argument adapter retains explicit null/scalar/vector handling and the Swing RGB adapter reads its actual components. The duplicate stand-in type and generated stale class were removed.

Unequipped armor adapter: PreviewVanillaModel keeps the nullable visibility override from OMP VanillaPart/VanillaGroupPart separately from player skin geometry; the preview does not render equipped armor.

Root hierarchy adapter: PreviewFiguraParts exposes models:getChildren using OMP FiguraModelPart.getChildren semantics: a fresh 1-based table referencing the actual root parts. Existing named root access and pairs(models) enumeration remain available.
